scheme_name: PMMSY: Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana or PMMSY is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme is designed to promote sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector in India. 

The PMMSY aims to enhance fish production and productivity in the country. 

The scheme has a specific focus on increasing the income of fishers and fish farmers. 

It also aims to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY has a total outlay of ₹20,050 crores for a period of five years from 2020 to 2025. 

One of the key components of PMMSY is the establishment of Live Fish Vending Centres. 

The Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme is specifically aimed at improving the availability of fresh fish in urban areas. 

This initiative is particularly significant for states like Haryana where fish consumption is on the rise. 

The objective of the Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme is to set up modern vending centres. 

These centres will facilitate the sale of live fish to consumers. 

The scheme aims to ensure that fish is available at affordable prices. 

It also aims to reduce the post-harvest losses of fish. 

The Live Fish Vending Centres will be equipped with modern facilities. 

These facilities will include aerated tanks for storing live fish. 

The centres will also have proper sanitation and hygiene measures in place. 

The scheme targets to establish approximately 1,000 Live Fish Vending Centres across the country. 

In Haryana, the focus will be on urban areas with high demand for fresh fish. 

The benefits of the Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme include increased income for fish farmers. 

It will also provide consumers with access to fresh and live fish. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the livelihoods of fishers and fish vendors. 

The estimated financial assistance for setting up each Live Fish Vending Centre is around ₹5 lakhs. 

This financial assistance will cover the cost of infrastructure and equipment. 

The eligibility criteria for setting up a Live Fish Vending Centre include being a registered fish farmer or fish vendor. 

Applicants must have prior experience in fish vending or aquaculture. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants under this scheme. 

However, they must possess the necessary skills and knowledge related to fish handling and vending. 

The application process for the Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme involves several steps. 

Interested applicants must submit a detailed project proposal to the concerned fisheries department. 

The proposal should include the location and design of the vending centre. 

Applicants are required to provide proof of registration as a fish farmer or vendor. 

They must also submit identity proof and address proof documents. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be reviewed by the fisheries department. 

If approved, the applicant will receive a letter of sanction. 

The disbursement of funds will be made in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The first installment will be released upon approval of the project. 

Subsequent installments will be released after verification of the completed work. 

The implementation of the Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme will be overseen by the Department of Fisheries in Haryana. 

The department will be responsible for monitoring the progress of the centres. 

They will also ensure compliance with the guidelines set forth by the PMMSY. 

The scheme is expected to have a significant impact on the local economy. 

It will create job opportunities for local youth in urban areas. 

The availability of fresh fish will also promote better nutrition among consumers. 

The government aims to increase fish production in Haryana from 1.5 lakh tonnes to 2.5 lakh tonnes by 2025. 

The PMMSY also includes various other components such as aquaculture and fisheries infrastructure development. 

The scheme promotes the use of modern technology in fish farming. 

It encourages the adoption of sustainable fishing practices. 

The PMMSY also aims to enhance the quality of fish through better breeding techniques. 

The scheme is aligned with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme is a step towards achieving this goal. 

It is also expected to contribute to the overall growth of the fisheries sector in India. 

The government has set a target of creating 15 lakh jobs in the fisheries sector by 2025. 

The PMMSY will play a crucial role in achieving this target. 

The scheme is also expected to attract investments in the fisheries sector. 

The establishment of Live Fish Vending Centres will create a new market for fish farmers. 

It will also encourage more people to take up fish farming as a viable livelihood option. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive scheme that addresses various challenges faced by the fisheries sector. 

It aims to promote sustainable practices while ensuring economic growth. 

The Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme is an innovative solution to improve fish accessibility. 

It is a significant initiative for enhancing the livelihoods of fishers and vendors in Haryana. 

The scheme is expected to be a game-changer in the fisheries sector. 

It will ensure that consumers have access to fresh fish while supporting local economies. 

The PMMSY is a testament to the government's commitment to the development of the fisheries sector. 

It reflects the importance of fisheries in India's agricultural landscape. 

The Live Fish Vending Centres Scheme is a vital component of this larger vision. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable fisheries sector in India. 

The success of this scheme will depend on effective implementation and monitoring. 

The government encourages all eligible individuals to take advantage of this opportunity. 

The PMMSY is a significant step towards transforming the fisheries sector in India.
